hits.snippet: # RoboStore Launches Robo Inc\., a New Robotics Company for U\.S\. Robotics Deployment and Systems Integration RoboStore launches Robo Inc\. to support U\.S\. robotics deployment through manufacturing, systems integration, testing, security, and customized solutions for organizations\. RoboStore/YTScreenshot RoboStore has launched Robo Inc\., a new U\.S\.-based robotics company focused on manufacturing, deployment, and systems integration\. The launch gives RoboStore a broader role in helping organizations move from purchasing robot hardware to putting complete systems into practical use\. ## RoboStore Builds a New Path for Robot Deployment RoboStore has already built experience as a North American distributor and technology partner for Unitree platforms\. Its offerings include humanoid and quadruped robots, technical support, training, and custom solutions\. The new company was introduced publicly on August 10, 2026, after operating in stealth for about a year\. As reported by The Robot Report, Robo Inc\. is being positioned as a New York-based manufacturer and integrator that will support U\.S\. organizations with local engineering, integration, testing, and deployment services\.

# Facing Ban, US Seller of Chinese Robots Makes Domestic Manufacturing Push RoboStore, a major distributor of Chinese-made robots, is pushing to manufacture its systems domestically following the US ban on foreign-made advanced robots\. New York-based RoboStore has been selling humanoid and dog-like robots from Chinese vendor Unitree\. But on Monday, it launched Robo Incorporated, a US-based manufacturing and systems integration company\. “As the US races to strengthen domestic manufacturing and secure critical technologies, Robo Inc\. will open a 66,000-square-foot facility on Long Island, New York, which is expected to be fully operational by Q1 2027,” the company said\. Although humanoid robots are an emerging market, you may have seen them on social media, at trade shows, or at company events\. RoboStore notes that it’s sold and deployed “more than 1,500 humanoid and quadruped robots while serving 4,500 customers,” including Nvidia, Amazon, and Harvard University\. The company’s website sells a whole catalog of Unitree models, ranging from $10,000 to $20,000 to higher-end machines costing over $100,000\. # Robo Inc\. Launches US Humanoid Robot Integrator; China Spy Law Still Follows Hardware Roboinc\.com RoboStore, North America's most active distributor of humanoid and quadruped robots, today publicly launched **Robo Inc\.**, a US-based manufacturing and systems integration company designed to fill the compliance gap left by the Federal Communications Commission's July 28 decision to block new Chinese-made advanced robots from the American market\. The company says it will open a 66,000-square-foot \(roughly 6,130 square meters\) facility on Long Island, New York, expected to be operational by January 2027 — a concrete deadline and a named address in a sector that has historically offered neither\. The launch arrives at a moment when the American robotics market is genuinely stuck\. Chinese manufacturers currently account for approximately 51 percent of global humanoid robot production, with companies like Unitree offering fully operational humanoids starting at $13,500 — a price that domestic American manufacturers cannot match\. **California Dairies, Inc\.** has opened a new beverage manufacturing facility in Bakersfield, California\. The company, which is the largest dairy farmer-owned cooperative in California, invested in the 200,000 square-foot greenfield facility to meet growing demand for fluid milk products and has created 90 new full-time jobs\. The facility, named Valley Natural Beverages \(VNB\), sits on land that will allow for future expansion to 400,000 square feet\. It will begin by processing an estimated 116,000 gallons of locally sourced milk each day\. The plant features robotics, energy-efficient systems, and incorporates renewable energy sources and waste conservation measures to support environmental sustainability\. VNB will open with three processing lines dedicated to conventional extended shelf life \(ESL\) and ultra-high temperature \(UHT\) dairy beverages\. Supplement and vitamin maker NBTY Inc\. on Wednesday is scheduled to open a new manufacturing facility in a former Amityville warehouse to produce sports and nutritional bars\. The 66,000 square-foot plant will produce roughly 1 million bars a day, under the brand names Pure Protein, Good ‘n Natural Bars and Met-Rx\. The company broke ground on the facility in 2011, with help from $750,000 in state funding\. It will create an estimated 150 jobs\. NBTY, based in Ronkonkoma, employees roughly 14,000 people, including about 2,500 on Long Island\. The once public company was purchased in 2010 for $3\.8 billion by The Carlyle Group, a private equity firm based in Washington, D\.C\.

# Biopharmaceutical firm plans to close one of its Bay Area plants, lay off 25 A biopharmaceutical company operating in Vacaville for 24 years plans to close one of its two research and development facilities there\. This comes after a few years after it bought local land for expansion\. DesigneRx Pharmaceuticals Inc\., part of the U\.S\. arm of the Cayman Islands-based, Taiwan-anchored Polaris Group, notified state and local officials July 20 that it wants to end manufacturing at 4941 Allison Parkway, Suite B, affecting 25 workers\. Those layoffs there are set to start Sept\. 21 and end by mid-October, according to the filing\. Roughly five employees will remain there to decommission the facility and eventually turn it over the the building owner, the document said\.
